bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4806206615453696 Project: poppler Fuzzer: libFuzzer_poppler_pdf_fuzzer Fuzz target binary: pdf_fuzzer Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_poppler Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash Address: Crash State: CharCodeToUnicode::parseCMap1 CharCodeToUnicode::parseCMap GfxFont::readToUnicodeCMap Sanitizer: memory (MSAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=libfuzzer_msan_poppler&range=201808300320:201808310301 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=4806206615453696
bug_description.normalized: When Poppler renders the witness PDF, GfxFont::readToUnicodeCMap reads the attacker-controlled /ToUnicode stream and passes its bytes to CharCodeToUnicode::parseCMap1. That function allocates stack token buffers tok1/tok2/tok3 without initialization and reuses them across command dispatch. PSTokenizer::getToken only writes the token bytes plus a trailing NUL into tok2; the remaining stack bytes stay indeterminate. The malformed /ToUnicode CMap in the PoC yields a short outer-loop token, after which parseCMap1 dispatches on tok2 using strcmp against fixed string literals. At line 330, strcmp(tok2, "beginbfchar") is lowered to a fixed-size comparison of 12 bytes, so it reads past the initialized prefix into tok2's uninitialized tail. MemorySanitizer reports the first poisoned byte at offset 6 of that 12-byte read and identifies tok2's stack allocation in parseCMap1 as the origin.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled PDF /ToUnicode stream and materializes it into a GooString buffer for CMap parsing.
source.value_from: The witness PDF's font dictionary contains /ToUnicode 3 0 R; object 3 is the attacker-controlled stream read by fillGooString and then parsed as a ToUnicode CMap.

tainted_value_origin.description: tok2 is a stack buffer allocated without initialization. Only bytes explicitly written by PSTokenizer::getToken become defined; the untouched tail remains poisoned and is later read by strcmp.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. strcmp dispatch on the partially initialized stack token reads a 12-byte region while matching against the 11-character literal "beginbfchar" plus NUL, consuming uninitialized bytes from tok2's tail.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 6 inside a 12-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of tok2 in parseCMap1.

root_cause.description: The token dispatch buffer tok2 is stack-allocated without zero-initialization even though subsequent logic compares it to fixed keywords with strcmp after only partial writes from PSTokenizer::getToken.
root_cause.note: parseCMap1 relies on tok2 holding a NUL-terminated token, but it never initializes bytes beyond the current token length. When a malformed CMap produces a short token, strcmp on tok2 reads past the written bytes into the uninitialized stack tail. A correct fix would zero-initialize the token buffers before use or avoid fixed-length keyword comparisons on partially initialized storage.

parser_admitted.condition: obj1.isStream() is true for the witness PDF because the font dictionary's /ToUnicode entry points to stream object 3 0 R, so the function does not return early and proceeds to fillGooString/parseCMap.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer harness loads the witness PDF and renders its page, driving Poppler's font parsing logic.
The CID font loader finds a /ToUnicode stream, copies the attacker-controlled stream bytes into a GooString, and hands them to CharCodeToUnicode::parseCMap.

parseCMap1 tokenizes the malformed CMap into uninitialized stack buffers and dispatches on tok2 with strcmp; the beginbfchar comparison reads tok2's uninitialized tail and MSAN reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Reads the attacker-controlled /ToUnicode PDF stream into GooString buf. The resulting byte sequence is the exact CMap payload later tokenized by parseCMap1.
Aliases the attacker-controlled GooString storage as a mutable char* cursor p and passes that cursor into parseCMap1, making the /ToUnicode bytes the tokenizer's input stream.
Allocates the stack token buffers without initialization. MSAN later identifies this allocation as the origin of the uninitialized bytes observed in tok2.

PSTokenizer copies the next attacker-controlled outer-loop token into tok2. getToken writes only the token bytes and one trailing NUL; for the malformed witness CMap, the token is shorter than the 11-byte keyword tested below, so tok2's remaining stack bytes stay uninitialized.

No guard checks that tok2 has enough initialized bytes for any fixed keyword comparison. For the witness token, the usecmap comparison is false, so control falls through and tok2 is immediately reused in the next strcmp-based dispatch.

MSAN sink. strcmp on tok2 is lowered to a fixed-size comparison against "beginbfchar\0", reading 12 bytes from tok2. Because step 4 initialized only the token prefix, the compare reaches uninitialized stack bytes in tok2's tail; the sanitizer reports the first poisoned byte at offset 6 of this 12-byte read.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of tok2 in the stack frame of parseCMap1; the actual tok2 declaration is line 306.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from ARVO vulnerable Docker sanitizer_trace.txt

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix_commit/patch.diff do not modify poppler/CharCodeToUnicode.cc or related ToUnicode tokenization code. The provided patch bundle is therefore unrelated to the witnessed MSAN crash and does not demonstrate the actual fix for this bug.

poc.trigger: The witness is an 839-byte PDF 1.7 file with a Type0 CID font whose dictionary contains /ToUnicode 3 0 R. Object 3 is a malformed FlateDecode stream; when Poppler reads it as a ToUnicode CMap during page rendering, parseCMap1 receives a short outer-loop token in tok2 and then crashes in strcmp(tok2, "beginbfchar").

format.name: PDF with ToUnicode CMap stream
format.contract: A PDF whose font /ToUnicode stream is malformed so that CharCodeToUnicode::parseCMap1 tokenizes an outer-loop command token into tok2 that is shorter than the fixed keyword "beginbfchar". Because tok2 is a reused uninitialized stack buffer and only the token prefix plus NUL are written, the subsequent strcmp-based dispatch reads uninitialized tail bytes and triggers MSAN.
